---

**R1: W-Critical-1 — Base-model-only scope framing 过宽**
- 审稿意见：Abstract "When LLM outputs re-enter generation pipelines..." 过于宽泛，可能误导
- 现状：Abstract line 7 已有 "restricted to base models"，Introduction line 6 已有 scope qualifier
- 方案：(a) Abstract 首句改为明确限定 base-model scope，如 "When base-model LLM outputs re-enter generation pipelines..."；(b) 检查 Conclusion 是否有未限定的宽泛表述
- 判断：Writing fix，可立即执行

**R2: W-Critical-2 — "formalize" 改为 "characterize"**
- 审稿意见：全文无 DDR 数学定义，"formalize" 名不副实
- 方案：全局搜索 "formalize/formalization"，替换为 "characterize/characterization"
- 判断：R2 说 major (writing fix)，合理。可立即执行

**R3: W-Critical-3 — 新颖性 vs model collapse 定位模糊**
- 审稿意见：DDR 核心观察在 model collapse 文献已有讨论，Introduction 将其包装为全新发现
- 现状：Introduction P2 已有 "Concurrent work characterizes convergence..."，Discussion 已区分 DDR vs model collapse
- 方案：(a) Introduction 坦诚承认 distributional compression 是已知现象，DDR 贡献在于 precision decomposition (location vs shape) + cross-generator detection application；(b) 具体改写 Introduction P2 开头，从 "We introduce" 改为 "Building on documented distributional compression under recursive generation, we identify and characterize..."
- 请 Reviewer 审查：这个定位调整是否削弱了 contribution，还是让 positioning 更诚实从而更可信？

---

## Should-Fix

**R4: W-Major-1 — 3-class 分辨率 overclaim**
- 现状：Abstract line 6 已有 "effective resolution: three depth classes"
- 方案：已解决，无需进一步修改
- 请 Reviewer 确认

**R5: W-Major-2 — Continuation-chain vs 真实递归场景差距**
- 审稿意见：未覆盖 instruction-following chains、multi-turn 对话、混合模型链等
- 方案：Discussion 新增 1-2 句，明确说明 continuation-chain 与真实场景的差异及其对结果的影响
- 草案："Our generation chains use open-ended continuation prompts; real-world recursive pipelines—instruction-following chains, multi-turn dialogues, mixed-model editing—impose additional constraints that may either attenuate or restructure the DDR pattern. Extending beyond laboratory chains remains an open challenge."

**R6: W-Major-3 — Cohen's d threshold sensitivity**
- 审稿意见：drifting 边界 |d|>0.6 无理论依据，未做 sensitivity analysis
- 现状：Appendix V DDR Partition Validation 已有 exhaustive enumeration (35 possible splits)、permutation test (p=0.030)、ε sweep [0.10, 0.75]
- 方案：Results §4.2 Validation 段已引用 "invariant for ε∈[0.10,0.75]"。补充一句解释 drifting threshold 来自 clustering (k=2 silhouette=0.660)，不是手工设定
- 判断：Writing fix，现有数据已覆盖。不需补实验。请 Reviewer 核实

**R7: W-Major-4 — 7 特征选择缺系统化论证**
- 审稿意见：未报告初始候选集和筛选过程
- 方案：§3.3 开头加 1-2 句说明特征选择理由——从 NLL distribution summary statistics (mean, std, max, min) + tail structure (tail_decay) 覆盖 distributional moments，加 surface diversity (TTR, hapax) 作为 reference-free complement。非穷举搜索，而是 principled coverage of distributional properties
- 请 Reviewer 审查措辞是否足够

**R8: W-Major-5 — 负面结果过度依赖附录**
- 现状：Discussion 已包含 instruct 关键数字（silhouette 0.660→0.372, ρ 反转, 3-class F1 下降 3.7-19.9pp, QLoRA 恢复 0.89-0.91）
- Cross-domain 结果（F1 0.62-0.65）尚未在正文提及
- 方案：Discussion 加一句 cross-domain 结果引用："Cross-domain evaluation (BookCorpus, CC-News) yields binary F1\,=\,0.74--0.75 but inverted 3-class F1 (0.62--0.65; Appendix J), reflecting calibration loss at the gen-0/gen-1 boundary while preserving the gen-1/gen-2+ depth signal."

---

## Minor

**R9: W-Minor-1 — Pages 1-3 无 display item**
- 现状：Table 1 (features) 在 page 4
- 方案：受限于 8 页限制和当前 section 结构，很难把 Figure 1 前移到 p2-3 不影响内容流。Feature table 在 p4 已部分缓解。可尝试把 Figure 1 (DDR trajectory) 用 figure* 提前到 Results 开头
- 请 Reviewer 评估是否值得重新排列——风险是打乱当前已平衡的 float 布局

**R10: W-Minor-2 — 术语一致性**
- 方案：统一用 "generation depth" (不再交替用 "recursive generation depth")；DDR 明确区分 pattern vs partition 用法
- Writing fix

**R11: W-Minor-3 — Table 3 出现在 Table 2 之前**
- 这是 LaTeX float positioning 问题
- 方案：检查 table 定义位置和 float specifier，确保编号顺序匹配出现顺序

**R12: W-Minor-4 — Granger 因果仅 5 时间点**
- 方案：Discussion 中 Granger 引用改为 "supplementary evidence" 而非核心论证；或加 caveat "limited by chain length"

---

## Missing References

**R13: MR1 — Pillutla et al. (2021) MAUVE**
- 真实论文，NeurIPS 2021。Distribution gap metric，与 DDR location drift 相关
- 方案：Related Work §2.3 或 Method §3.3 中引用

**R14: MR2 — Briesch et al. (2023)**
- 上一轮 Reviewer 已确认 4 次 WebSearch 找不到，大概率审稿人幻觉
- 方案：不添加

**R15: MR3 — Diaz & Karampatziakis (2019)**
- 实际是 Diaz & Marathe (CVPR 2019)，vision 领域 ordinal regression
- 方案：关联性有限，不添加

**R16: MR4 — Tulchinskii et al. (2024)**
- 已在 Related Work §2.1 以 intrinsic_dim_detection 引用
- 方案：已解决

---

## Layout Issues

**R17: Pages 22-23 间距问题（用户直接指出 2219-2220 行）**
- Feature Distribution 部分 Figure 8/9 与文字间大量留白
- 方案：调整 float specifier，确保图文紧密排列

**R18: Page 33 Z.6 排版**

% Responds to R35-W2 / R38 concern about drifting boundary sensitivity.

\paragraph{Threshold sensitivity.}
To address concerns about the sensitivity of the drifting-boundary threshold,
we sweep $|d|$ from $0.10$ to $0.80$ in increments of $0.05$ and record the
resulting binary partition (drifting vs.\ stationary) along with the silhouette
score in standardised $(\lvert\rho\rvert, d)$ space.
Across the entire range, only \emph{three} distinct partitions emerge,
reflecting natural gaps between feature clusters rather than threshold artefacts.
The three-feature drifting set (\textsc{entropy\_mean}, \textsc{ttr}, \textsc{hapax\_ratio})
is stable across $|d| \in [0.50,\, 0.75]$ with a silhouette of $0.66$---the
peak value in the sweep.
Including the intermediate feature \textsc{entropy\_std} ($d = 0.49$) yields a
4/3 partition stable across $|d| \in [0.10,\, 0.45]$ (silhouette $= 0.45$).
The partition used in our analysis corresponds to the peak-silhouette region,
confirming that the drifting--stationary boundary reflects a natural gap in the
$(\lvert\rho\rvert, d)$ landscape rather than an artefact of a particular
threshold choice.

We evaluate whether depth signal generalizes beyond Wikipedia by constructing generation chains from three additional domains: News articles, Academic abstracts, and Code documentation.
For each domain, we sample 200 seed texts and generate chains of depth 3 using three generators (Pythia-1B, Qwen3-1.7B, Mistral-7B).
The same 7-feature ensemble and LOGO protocol are applied.

\noindent\textbf{Important caveat:} Cross-domain generation used $t{=}1.0$, top-$p{=}1.0$, which falls outside the method's reliable operating range ($t \leq 0.7$; Appendix~\ref{app:sampling-sensitivity}). Domain and temperature effects are therefore confounded in the results below; the cross-domain signal may partly reflect temperature-induced distributional divergence rather than domain generalization alone.

\begin{table}[ht]
\centering
\small
\caption{Cross-domain depth classification under LOGO evaluation (binary: gen-1 vs.\ gen-2+). Three generators $\times$ 200 seeds per domain. Bootstrap 95\% CIs ($n$\,=\,1000).}
\label{tab:domain}
\begin{tabular}{lccc}
\toprule
\textbf{Domain} & \textbf{Binary F1} & \textbf{95\% CI} & \textbf{3-class F1} \\
\midrule
Code           & 0.754 & [0.737, 0.770] & 0.634 \\
News           & 0.746 & [0.726, 0.764] & 0.652 \\
Academic       & 0.739 & [0.720, 0.757] & 0.622 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

All three non-Wikipedia domains achieve binary F1 $>$ 0.73 under leave-one-generator-out evaluation, which demonstrates that depth signal is not an artifact of Wikipedia text properties.

\paragraph{Domain $\times$ temperature interaction.}
Cross-domain generation used $t{=}1.0$, top-$p{=}1.0$ (vs.\ the main experiment's $t{=}0.7$, top-$p{=}0.9$).
Supplementary evaluation at $t{=}0.7$ reveals a domain $\times$ temperature interaction: the main Wikipedia experiment favors lower temperature (depth signal degrades monotonically with rising temperature; Appendix~\ref{app:sampling-sensitivity}), while cross-domain evaluation favors higher temperature ($t{=}1.0$ yields +3 to +11\,pp over $t{=}0.7$; News 0.746 vs.\ 0.712, Academic 0.739 vs.\ 0.628, Code 0.754 vs.\ 0.687).
This asymmetry likely reflects reference-model calibration: Pythia-410M, trained predominantly on web text, detects subtle per-step drift in Wikipedia but requires larger distributional divergence (produced by higher temperature) to detect depth signal in out-of-distribution domains.
This finding suggests that reference model selection is a key factor for cross-domain deployment of depth profiling.

\paragraph{3-class inversion as DDR evidence.}
In the cross-domain setting, 3-class F1 (0.62--0.65) falls below binary F1 (0.74--0.75), reversing the pattern observed in the main experiment (3-class 0.762 $>$ binary 0.694).
This inversion reflects degraded gen-0 vs.\ gen-1 separation: the Pythia-410M reference model is calibrated to Wikipedia text, so its baseline entropy estimates are less discriminative for out-of-domain human text and compresses the feature distance between gen-0 and gen-1.
The binary task (gen-1 vs.\ gen-2+) is unaffected because both classes are generated under identical domain and decoding conditions; recursive drift is a relative change that does not depend on absolute calibration.
This pattern provides additional evidence that DDR captures base-model generation dynamics rather than domain-specific text properties: depth signal remains robust even when the human-vs-machine boundary becomes less distinct.

1	\section{Introduction}
2	\label{sec:introduction}
3	
4	AI text detection asks a single binary question---\emph{human or machine?}---and recent methods answer it with increasing reliability \cite{detectgpt,fast_detectgpt,binoculars,ld_score}.
5	Yet this framing elides a richer structure emerging on the open web: as LLM outputs re-enter training corpora \cite{dolma,fineweb} and seed further generation, text accumulates at varying \emph{recursive depths}---an estimated 7--17\% of recent scientific publications already contain substantial LLM-modified content \cite{mapping_llm_science,monitoring_ai_review}---and each generation cycle pushes distributional properties further from both the human source and the first-generation predecessor.
6	While most deployed LLM outputs use instruction-tuned models, base-model generation pipelines remain prevalent in synthetic data production, pre-training corpus construction, and recursive data augmentation; we accordingly scope this study to base (pretrained) models.
7	Knowing \emph{how many times} text has been recursively generated matters for data provenance \cite{ccnet,dsir} and model collapse analysis \cite{curse_of_recursion,strong_model_collapse}, yet no current method moves beyond the binary boundary.
8	
9	Distributional compression under recursive generation is well-documented \cite{curious_decline,broken_telephone,markovian_chains}.
10	We introduce \emph{depth fingerprinting}---classifying text by ordinal generation depth (gen-0\,/\,gen-1\,/\,gen-2+)---and decompose this compression into structurally distinct components: across eight base-model generators spanning five architectural families (0.6B--8B), the NLL distribution's central tendency (mean entropy, lexical diversity) drifts monotonically with depth while its shape (entropy extremes, tail structure) remains an order of magnitude more stable ($d{=}0.76$--$1.17$ vs.\ $d < 0.10$; convergence across parametric and non-parametric effect-size measures confirms this partition).
11	We term this location/shape asymmetry the \emph{differential depth response} (DDR)---a structural property of fixed-parameter autoregressive sampling that is mechanistically distinct from the tail-coverage erosion in model collapse \cite{curse_of_recursion} and analytically informative independent of both the specific mechanism and classification accuracy.
12	Where concurrent work characterizes \emph{that} and \emph{why} convergence occurs \cite{broken_telephone,markovian_chains}, DDR isolates \emph{what} converges from what is preserved, and leverages the stationary shape component for cross-generator depth prediction without per-generator calibration.
13	
14	As a proof of concept, a lightweight 7-feature ensemble informed by DDR achieves leak-free binary F1\,=\,0.694 under leave-one-generator-out evaluation, matching multi-detector ensembles at 2.4$\times$ lower inference cost; an end-to-end QLoRA classifier reaches 0.905 (6-gen LOGO; Appendix~\ref{app:qlora}), confirming that the depth signal extends well beyond handcrafted features.
15	
16	Our contributions:
17	\begin{enumerate}[nosep,leftmargin=*]
18	    \item \textbf{Empirical decomposition (DDR).} Clustering-based validation ($k{=}2$, silhouette\,=\,0.660) confirms that inference-chain drift separates into a drifting location component ($d{=}0.76$--$1.17$) and a stable shape component ($d < 0.10$). Where prior work documents \emph{what converges}---diversity loss \cite{curious_decline}, attractor dynamics \cite{markovian_chains}---DDR identifies \emph{what is preserved}: shape invariance provides the cross-generator reference needed for depth detection without per-generator calibration.

\section{Introduction}
\label{sec:introduction}

AI text detection asks a single binary question---\emph{human or machine?}---and recent methods answer it with increasing reliability \cite{detectgpt,fast_detectgpt,binoculars,ld_score}.
Yet this framing elides a richer structure emerging on the open web: as LLM outputs re-enter training corpora \cite{dolma,fineweb} and seed further generation, text accumulates at varying \emph{recursive depths}---an estimated 7--17\% of recent scientific publications already contain substantial LLM-modified content \cite{mapping_llm_science,monitoring_ai_review}---and each generation cycle pushes distributional properties further from both the human source and the first-generation predecessor.
While most deployed LLM outputs use instruction-tuned models, base-model generation pipelines remain prevalent in synthetic data production, pre-training corpus construction, and recursive data augmentation; we accordingly scope this study to base (pretrained) models.
Knowing \emph{how many times} text has been recursively generated matters for data provenance \cite{ccnet,dsir} and model collapse analysis \cite{curse_of_recursion,strong_model_collapse}, yet no current method moves beyond the binary boundary.

Distributional compression under recursive generation is well-documented \cite{curious_decline,broken_telephone,markovian_chains}.
We introduce \emph{depth fingerprinting}---classifying text by ordinal generation depth (gen-0\,/\,gen-1\,/\,gen-2+)---and decompose this compression into structurally distinct components: across eight base-model generators spanning five architectural families (0.6B--8B), the NLL distribution's central tendency (mean entropy, lexical diversity) drifts monotonically with depth while its shape (entropy extremes, tail structure) remains an order of magnitude more stable ($d{=}0.76$--$1.17$ vs.\ $d < 0.10$; convergence across parametric and non-parametric effect-size measures confirms this partition).
We term this location/shape asymmetry the \emph{differential depth response} (DDR)---a structural property of fixed-parameter autoregressive sampling that is mechanistically distinct from the tail-coverage erosion in model collapse \cite{curse_of_recursion} and analytically informative independent of both the specific mechanism and classification accuracy.
Where concurrent work characterizes \emph{that} and \emph{why} convergence occurs \cite{broken_telephone,markovian_chains}, DDR isolates \emph{what} converges from what is preserved, and leverages the stationary shape component for cross-generator depth prediction without per-generator calibration.

As a proof of concept, a lightweight 7-feature ensemble informed by DDR achieves leak-free binary F1\,=\,0.694 under leave-one-generator-out evaluation, matching multi-detector ensembles at 2.4$\times$ lower inference cost; an end-to-end QLoRA classifier reaches 0.905 (6-gen LOGO; Appendix~\ref{app:qlora}), confirming that the depth signal extends well beyond handcrafted features.

Our contributions:
\begin{enumerate}[nosep,leftmargin=*]
    \item \textbf{Empirical decomposition (DDR).} Clustering-based validation ($k{=}2$, silhouette\,=\,0.660) confirms that inference-chain drift separates into a drifting location component ($d{=}0.76$--$1.17$) and a stable shape component ($d < 0.10$). Where prior work documents \emph{what converges}---diversity loss \cite{curious_decline}, attractor dynamics \cite{markovian_chains}---DDR identifies \emph{what is preserved}: shape invariance provides the cross-generator reference needed for depth detection without per-generator calibration.
    \item \textbf{Task formulation and evaluation suite.} We define generation depth classification as an ordinal prediction task and construct a controlled dataset of 37K texts from eight generators across five families (0.6B--8B), with leave-one-generator-out cross-validation as the primary evaluation protocol.
\end{enumerate}
A proof-of-concept classifier and systematic boundary mapping across temperature, prompt type, instruction tuning, and model scale establish where DDR-based detection succeeds and where it fails.

\section{Introduction}
\label{sec:introduction}

AI text detection asks a single binary question---\emph{human or machine?}---and recent methods answer it with increasing reliability \cite{detectgpt,fast_detectgpt,binoculars,ld_score}.
Yet this framing elides a richer structure emerging on the open web: as LLM outputs re-enter training corpora \cite{dolma,fineweb} and seed further generation, text accumulates at varying \emph{recursive depths}---an estimated 7--17\% of recent scientific publications already contain substantial LLM-modified content \cite{mapping_llm_science,monitoring_ai_review}---and each generation cycle pushes distributional properties further from both the human source and the first-generation predecessor.
While most deployed LLM outputs use instruction-tuned models, base-model generation pipelines remain prevalent in synthetic data production, pre-training corpus construction, and recursive data augmentation; we accordingly scope this study to base (pretrained) models.
Knowing \emph{how many times} text has been recursively generated matters for data provenance \cite{ccnet,dsir} and model collapse analysis \cite{curse_of_recursion,strong_model_collapse}, yet no current method moves beyond the binary boundary.

We introduce \emph{depth fingerprinting}: classifying text by ordinal generation depth (gen-0\,/\,gen-1\,/\,gen-2+) and decomposing the distributional drift that accumulates across depths into structurally distinct components.
The core empirical finding is a \emph{differential depth response} (DDR): across eight base-model generators spanning five architectural families (0.6B--8B), the NLL distribution's central tendency (mean entropy, lexical diversity) drifts monotonically with depth while its shape (entropy extremes, tail structure) remains an order of magnitude more stable ($d{=}0.76$--$1.17$ vs.\ $d < 0.10$; convergence across parametric and non-parametric effect-size measures confirms this partition).
This location/shape asymmetry exposes a structural property of fixed-parameter autoregressive sampling: the decoding mechanism systematically compresses where the output distribution sits while preserving its higher-order form---a pattern mechanistically distinct from the tail-coverage erosion in model collapse \cite{curse_of_recursion}, and analytically informative independent of both the specific mechanism and classification accuracy.
Concurrent work characterizes convergence in paraphrastic and translation chains \cite{broken_telephone,markovian_chains}; ours is the first to decompose the drift into complementary location and shape components and to leverage this asymmetry for cross-generator depth prediction.
We restrict to base (pretrained) models to isolate the generation dynamics from alignment artifacts (\S\ref{sec:discussion}).

As a proof of concept, a lightweight 7-feature ensemble informed by DDR achieves leak-free binary F1\,=\,0.694 under leave-one-generator-out evaluation, surpassing individual detection baselines by 6.7--36.3\,pp; an end-to-end QLoRA classifier reaches 0.905 (6-gen LOGO; Appendix~\ref{app:qlora}), confirming that the depth signal extends well beyond handcrafted features.

Our contributions:
\begin{enumerate}[nosep,leftmargin=*]
    \item \textbf{Empirical decomposition (DDR).} Clustering-based validation ($k{=}2$, silhouette\,=\,0.660) confirms that inference-chain drift separates into a drifting location component ($d{=}0.76$--$1.17$) and a stable shape component ($d < 0.10$). Where prior work documents \emph{what converges}---diversity loss \cite{curious_decline}, attractor dynamics \cite{markovian_chains}---DDR identifies \emph{what is preserved}: shape invariance provides the cross-generator reference needed for depth detection without per-generator calibration.
    \item \textbf{Task formulation and evaluation suite.} We define generation depth classification as an ordinal prediction task and construct a controlled dataset of 37K texts from eight generators across five families (0.6B--8B), with leave-one-generator-out cross-validation as the primary evaluation protocol.
\end{enumerate}
We additionally provide a proof-of-concept classifier (binary F1\,=\,0.694) and systematically map its operating boundaries across temperature, prompt type, instruction tuning, and model scale, establishing where DDR-based detection succeeds and where it fails.
